sentences.text: Ch.Badraiah vs State Of Ap on 18 September, 2019

Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5499 Of 2019
Order:

1. The petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 seek to quash the proceedings against them in C.C. No.242 of 2018, pending on the file of learned Additional Junior Civil Judge, Chilakaluripet, Guntur district (for short, 'the trial Court), which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 188, 272,
273, 420 and 120-B of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Additional Junior Civil Judge, Chilakaluripet, Guntur district
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that, on 07.03.2018 at 02.00 P.M., on receiving the credible information, the complainant suo motu registered the case against the petitioners and A-3 on the ground that they are in possession of the banned tobacco products, having purchased the same from an unknown person, selling the same to innocent public in their buddy shops at higher price deteriorating their health condition and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same and registered F.I.R. for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR and UDPR,J filing charge sheet is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of the Head Constable, Chilakaluripeta Town Police Station.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

pending on the file learned Additional Junior Civil Judge, Chilakaluripet, which was taken cognizance for the aforesaid offences.
6.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
